title: Integral Specht Modules and Modular Simple Modules

items.title: Integral Specht lattice and base change
items.statement: For every partition λ of n≥0, let M_Z^λ be the free abelian group on λ-tabloids and S_Z^λ its Z[S_n]-submodule generated by integral column polytabloids. Standard polytabloids form a Z-basis of S_Z^λ; for every commutative ring R, S_R^λ := R⊗_Z S_Z^λ embeds as the polytabloid span in M_R^λ. The empty shape gives a rank-one lattice.
items.strategy: Use the published left-action tableaux and integral ±1 coefficients to define M_Z and e_t. Re-run finite Garnir straightening with its explicit ±1 coefficients: the published complex Garnir relation is an integral vector identity because M_Z injects into M_C, so no division by a column-subgroup order is made in R. Its descending finite tableau order gives integral spanning. The published leading-tabloid coefficient 1 gives integral independence and a unit triangular minor; hence S_Z is saturated and a direct Z-summand of M_Z. Tensor the split inclusion with arbitrary R, including rings of characteristic p, and identify the images with the R-polytabloids.

items.title: Integral tabloid form and Specht Gram matrix
items.statement: The tabloid basis of M_Z^λ has the S_n-invariant symmetric Z-bilinear form (T,U)=δ_{T,U}. Its restriction to S_Z^λ has the integer Gram matrix G_λ in the standard-polytabloid basis. Tensoring this form and matrix with a commutative ring R defines the corresponding bilinear forms and G_λ over R; positivity is asserted only after embedding in R or C, not in characteristic p.
items.strategy: Define the form by its orthonormal tabloid basis, check invariance because S_n permutes tabloids, and check κ_t is self-adjoint because inverse and sign preserve C_t. Restrict along the integral standard basis from the preceding item. Every entry is an integer sum of products of ±1 coefficients; scalar extension reproduces the same Gram matrix over R. Distinguish this bilinear construction from the published complex Hermitian form, whose conjugation and positivity cannot be reduced modulo p.

items.title: Modular Specht form and radical quotient
items.statement: Fix prime p and a splitting p-modular system (K,O,k) for S_n. On S_k^λ=k⊗_Z S_Z^λ use the reduced integral tabloid bilinear form. Its form radical R^λ=S_k^λ∩(S_k^λ)^⊥ inside M_k^λ is an S_n-submodule. Define D^λ=S_k^λ/R^λ, allowing D^λ=0. R^λ is a form radical; equality with the module radical is a later consequence when D^λ is nonzero.
items.strategy: Use scalar extension of the integral basis and form, so the definition is independent of any lift of vectors. Invariance makes the orthogonal complement stable and therefore its intersection with S_k stable. Form the quotient in k[S_n]-modules and record that its dimension is rank_k(G_λ mod p). Do not infer simplicity or identify this kernel with the module radical before the field submodule theorem.

items.title: Field antisymmetrizers have rank-one own-shape image and detect dominance
items.statement: For any field F and partitions λ,µ of n, κ_t M_F^λ=F e_t with e_t≠0. If κ_t M_F^µ≠0, then λ dominates µ. The statements include characteristic two and n=0.
items.strategy: Re-express the published combinatorial column-collision and tableau-matching proofs as identities with coefficients 0, ±1 in the integral tabloid basis. Thus a λ-tabloid is either killed by κ_t or sent to ±e_t; the coefficient of {t} in e_t is 1 over every field. If a µ-tabloid survives, it has at most one element of each column of t in every row; the published basic tableau lemma gives λ⊒µ. No averaging or division by a group order occurs.

items.title: James submodule theorem over every field
items.statement: For any field F, λ⊢n, and F[S_n]-submodule U≤M_F^λ, either S_F^λ≤U or U≤(S_F^λ)^⊥ for the bilinear tabloid form. Consequently S_F^λ/(S_F^λ∩(S_F^λ)^⊥) is zero or absolutely irreducible and self-dual; when nonzero the form radical is the unique maximal submodule and equals the module radical.
items.strategy: If κ_t U is nonzero for one tableau t, the rank-one-image lemma puts e_t in U; its S_n-orbit generates S_F^λ. Otherwise self-adjointness of every κ_t and e_t=κ_t{t} show U is perpendicular to every polytabloid. For a submodule of S, the two alternatives show every proper submodule lies in the form radical, so a nonzero quotient is simple and that radical is unique maximal. The induced symmetric invariant form on the quotient is nondegenerate, giving self-duality. The integer Gram matrix has unchanged rank after any field extension F→E; the same argument over E gives absolute irreducibility. The alternatives need not be exclusive when the form vanishes.

items.title: p-regular and p-restricted partitions
items.statement: For a prime p, λ is p-regular if each positive part occurs fewer than p times. It is p-restricted if λ_i−λ_{i+1}
items.strategy: The difference λ_i−λ_{i+1} counts columns of height exactly i, hence parts equal to i in λ′. Compare each difference with p. The empty partition satisfies both conditions. Keep James p-regular D^λ labels distinct from the p-restricted dual-Specht convention.

items.title: Specht Gram gcd detects p-regularity
items.statement: Let z_j count the rows of λ of length j and let g_λ be the positive gcd of all integer pairings (e_s,e_t) of integral polytabloids. The products L=∏_j z_j! and U=∏_j(z_j!)^j satisfy L|g_λ|U. In particular g_λ is nonzero modulo p exactly when λ is p-regular. For a tableau t and its row-reversal t*, (e_t,e_{t*})=U and κ_t e_{t*}=Ue_t over every field.
items.strategy: Group tabloids into row-shuffling classes; each common tabloid contributes a packet of size L, proving L divides every pairing. Reverse each row of t to obtain t*: match common tabloids by independent permutations of equal-length rows in each of their j columns and check the signs agree, giving exactly U common signed terms. This proves g divides U. L and U have the same prime divisors, so reduction of all Gram entries vanishes iff some z_j≥p. The rank-one antisymmetrizer image and self-adjointness turn the reversed-row pairing into the scalar κ_t e_{t*}=Ue_t, with coefficient checked at {t}. Empty products are 1.

items.title: Nonzero modular Specht quotient criterion
items.statement: For the fixed splitting field k of characteristic p, D^λ is nonzero if and only if λ is p-regular. For p-regular λ it is absolutely irreducible, self-dual, and the unique simple head of S_k^λ.
items.strategy: The quotient has dimension equal to rank_k G_λ. The Gram form is identically zero exactly when every integral Gram entry is divisible by p, equivalently p|g_λ; the gcd lemma makes this equivalent to p-singularity. For a nonzero quotient apply the field James theorem to obtain absolute simplicity, self-duality and the unique-head identification.

items.title: Nonzero maps into tabloid quotients force dominance
items.statement: Let λ,µ⊢n with λ p-regular and U≤M_k^µ. A nonzero k[S_n]-map φ:S_k^λ→M_k^µ/U implies λ⊒µ. If λ=µ, then Im φ=(S_k^µ+U)/U. The same dominance conclusion holds for a nonzero map from D^λ into M_k^µ/U.
items.strategy: Choose t and row-reversed t*. The gcd lemma gives κ_t e_{t*}=h e_t with h=∏_j(z_j!)^j nonzero in k. Since e_t generates S and φ is nonzero, φ(e_t)≠0, so applying κ_t to φ(e_{t*}) is nonzero. Thus κ_t M_k^µ≠0 and the field dominance lemma yields λ⊒µ. If λ=µ, the rank-one image forces φ(e_t) to be a scalar multiple of e_t+U; cyclic generation gives the exact image. A map from D^λ lifts along S_k^λ→D^λ by composition, so the same conclusion follows.

items.title: Modular simple modules of the symmetric group
items.statement: For every n≥0 and splitting field k of characteristic p, the D^λ indexed by p-regular λ⊢n form a complete, pairwise nonisomorphic family of absolutely irreducible k[S_n]-modules. They are precisely the nonzero radical quotients and unique simple heads of the corresponding Specht modules.
items.strategy: The nonzero quotient theorem gives absolute simplicity and the head property. If D^λ≅D^µ, compose S^λ→D^λ≅D^µ↪M^µ/R^µ and apply the dominance-map lemma to obtain λ⊒µ; reverse λ,µ and use antisymmetry. For exhaustion, p-regular permutations are exactly those whose disjoint-cycle lengths are prime to p, and conjugacy classes are indexed by cycle type. Compare the coefficient of x^n in ∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j+⋯+x^{(p−1)j})=∏_{p∤j}(1−x^j)^{−1} as a formal power series: it counts p-regular partitions and p-regular conjugacy classes equally. The published Brauer simple-count result for a splitting field gives the same total number of simple modules, so the constructed pairwise distinct family exhausts them. All counting at each coefficient is finite.

items.title: Dominance unitriangularity of the symmetric-group decomposition matrix
items.statement: Let rows be all λ⊢n, columns the p-regular µ⊢n, and d_{λµ}=[S_k^λ:D^µ] be the decomposition number obtained by reducing the integral Specht lattice of the ordinary irreducible over K. Then d_{λµ}=0 unless µ⊒λ, and d_{λλ}=1 for p-regular λ. Ordering p-regular rows first in decreasing lexicographic order gives a lower unitriangular leading square block. This is a constraint, not a formula for all entries.
items.strategy: First use the integral standard basis and characteristic-zero nondegenerate rational tabloid form to see K⊗S_Z^λ is an absolutely irreducible KG-module; O⊗S_Z^λ is a stable full lattice with reduction S_k^λ, so the published decomposition-map definition gives the stated d. For each composition factor D^ν of M^λ/S^λ, realize it in a quotient M^λ/U with U⊇S^λ; the dominance-map lemma gives ν⊒λ, and its equality clause rules out ν=λ. The ambient tabloid form is nondegenerate, so (S^λ)^⊥ is dual to M^λ/S^λ; all D^ν are self-dual, hence every factor of S^λ∩(S^λ)^⊥ has ν▷λ. The remaining quotient of S^λ is D^λ exactly when λ is p-regular, with multiplicity one. Dominance implies lexicographic precedence, giving the stated matrix orientation.

items.title: Conjugate Specht modules are sign-twisted duals over every field
items.statement: For any field F and λ⊢n, there is a natural F[S_n]-isomorphism S_F^λ⊗sgn ≅ (S_F^{λ′})*. It uses the James polytabloid convention and remains valid when the Specht form is degenerate.
items.strategy: Construct James’s integral equivariant epimorphism Φ_Z:M_Z^{λ′}→S_Z^λ⊗sgn by transposing a tableau and applying its signed row-symmetrizer; check that row-equivalent transposed tableaux give the same image and that transposed tabloids map onto the polytabloid generators. Over Q the characteristic-zero argument identifies ker Φ_Q with (S_Q^{λ′})^⊥. The integral standard-polytabloid basis has a unit leading-tabloid minor, so S_Z^{λ′} is saturated in M_Z^{λ′}; its orthogonal complement is a direct summand and commutes with base change. The epimorphism also has a free target, hence a split underlying Z-module sequence. These facts carry ker Φ=(S^{λ′})^⊥ through arbitrary F, including p dividing n!. The perfect ambient tabloid pairing identifies M_F^{λ′}/(S_F^{λ′})^⊥ with (S_F^{λ′})*, giving the isomorphism without assuming the restricted Specht form nondegenerate.

items.title: p-regular and p-restricted labels under transpose and sign
items.statement: For p-restricted µ, define the dual Specht module S(µ):=(S_k^µ)* and its cellular simple head D(µ). Then D(µ)≅D^{µ′}⊗sgn. Equivalently, for p-regular λ, D^λ≅D(λ′)⊗sgn. This is a q=1 group-side convention statement; sign is trivial in characteristic two but conjugation remains necessary.
items.strategy: The conjugate-Specht sign-duality lemma gives S_k^µ⊗sgn≅(S_k^{µ′})*. Dualize to identify S(µ) with S_k^{µ′}⊗sgn, using the finite-dimensional double-dual. As µ′ is p-regular, the unique head of S_k^{µ′} is D^{µ′}; tensoring with one-dimensional sign preserves heads and simplicity, so the head of S(µ) is D^{µ′}⊗sgn. Replace µ by λ′ for the equivalent formula. This explicitly defines the dual-Specht notation before later Hecke or branching consumers use it.

items.title: Triangularity does not compute every modular decomposition number
items.statement: The dominance-zero pattern and diagonal ones constrain the decomposition matrix but do not determine its remaining entries. Any stronger formula needs further hypotheses and proof; no general positive-characteristic decomposition algorithm is asserted here.
items.strategy: Compare the theorem’s allowed off-diagonal positions with the need to compute actual composition multiplicities. James §12 separates the triangular statement from the later calculation problem; the later Hecke/canonical-basis regime and positive-characteristic adjustment questions are distinct. This is a boundary remark, not a claimed theorem about the current state of every algorithm.

title: Integral Specht Modules and Modular Simple Modules — Examples

items.title: Specht Gram rank for shape (2,2)
items.statement: For λ=(2,2), the standard-polytabloid Gram matrix is [[4,2],[2,4]]. Its rank is 0 in characteristic 2, 1 in characteristic 3, and 2 in characteristic p>3; hence these are the dimensions of D^(2,2).
items.strategy: List the two standard tableaux, expand each signed column orbit in the tabloid basis, and calculate the four pairings to obtain [[4,2],[2,4]]. Reduce entries modulo 2 and 3; for p>3 use determinant 12 and nonzero diagonal. Invoke the quotient-rank identity from the modular-form definition. The p=2 Specht lattice still has rank two although its form quotient vanishes.

items.title: Decomposition matrices of S3 at p=2 and p=3
items.statement: With rows (3),(2,1),(1,1,1): at p=2, columns D^(3),D^(2,1) give [[1,0],[0,1],[1,0]]; at p=3, the same column labels give [[1,0],[1,1],[0,1]]. Both obey the stated dominance orientation.
items.strategy: Use S^(3)=trivial and S^(1^3)=sign. At p=2 the sign equals trivial while the two-dimensional standard Specht is simple; at p=3, the augmentation model of S^(2,1) contains the all-ones vector because 3=0, giving a trivial submodule and a sign quotient. Identify the p-regular labels by the nonzero Gram quotients and check the row dimensions and each composition factor. Compare with James Example 12.4.

items.title: p-regular and p-restricted labels differ
items.statement: For p=2, λ=(2) is p-regular but not p-restricted, whereas λ′=(1,1) is p-restricted but not p-regular. Thus a p-restricted good-node statement cannot be applied to the James label without the transpose/sign translation.
items.strategy: Check multiplicities of equal positive parts and the adjacent difference to zero directly for (2) and (1,1). Note that sign is trivial at p=2, so the required change of partition is visible even in that characteristic.

items.title: Modular Specht modules need not be simple, and form heads can vanish
items.statement: Two different failures occur: S_k^(2,1) is reducible in characteristic 3, while S_k^(2,2) is nonzero but its invariant form quotient D^(2,2) is zero in characteristic 2. The latter witness alone is not asserted to be reducible.
items.strategy: For p=3 identify S^(2,1) with the two-dimensional augmentation submodule of k^3; the all-ones vector lies in it and spans a proper trivial submodule, with sign quotient. For p=2 use the integral standard basis to show S^(2,2) has rank two, while a direct expansion of its Gram entries gives [[4,2],[2,4]]≡0. These independent calculations refute the respective ordinary extrapolations without making a false claim about simplicity of S^(2,2) in characteristic two.
